 The 2026 Tax Amnesty countdown: Don’t miss the deadline! 
 The 2026 Tax Amnesty countdown: Don’t miss the deadline!
 The 2026 Tax Amnesty Programme offers a 100% waiver of qualifying penalties, interest and fines. Taxpayers have until 31 December 2026 to regularise outstanding tax liabilities.
 5 Nov 2026 
 2 min read 
 Tax & Exchange Control Alert 
 Article 
 Authors
 Alex Kanyi
 Partner
 Tax & Exchange 
Control
 Moureen Tuya
 Trainee Advocate
 Related services
 Tax & Exchange 
Control 
 The Finance Act, 2026 (No. 19 of 2026) reintroduced the Tax Amnesty Programme by amending section 37E of the Tax Procedures Act, Cap. 469B. Specifically, section 45 of the Finance Act, 2026 extended the qualifying tax debt period from 31 December 2023 to 31 December 2025 and the deadline for settling outstanding principal tax from 30 June 2025 to 31 December 2026.
 The Programme took effect on 1 July 2026 and runs until 31 December 2026. It allows the Commissioner to refrain from recovering qualifying penalties, interest and fines relating to tax debts accrued up to 31 December 2025, subject to the statutory conditions.
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has also issued implementation guidance outlining the procedures for accessing the amnesty through the iTax portal.
 Eligibility Criteria and Exclusions
 Why taxpayers should take advantage of the amnesty program
 The 2026 Tax Amnesty Programme provides taxpayers with an opportunity to clear historical tax liabilities without bearing the accumulated penalties, interest and fines, provided the applicable conditions are met.
 Unlike an ordinary waiver application, which is subject to the applicable statutory conditions and the Commissioner’s discretion, the amnesty provides a specific statutory relief framework for qualifying historical tax debts.
 Our Comments
 The 2026 Tax Amnesty Programme provides a valuable opportunity for taxpayers to clear historical tax liabilities without the burden of accumulated qualifying penalties, interest and fines. Taxpayers should review their iTax ledgers, identify outstanding principal tax, file any missing returns and/or determine appropriate settlement arrangements.
 Upon meeting the applicable conditions, KRA will update the taxpayer’s ledger and issue an Amnesty Certificate through the taxpayer’s registered iTax email address. The certificate may also be accessed through the relevant iTax consultation and reprinting functionality.
 The deadline for the Programme is 31 December 2026, 55 days from the date of publication of this alert. Any qualifying principal tax that remains unpaid after this date will not benefit from the amnesty, and the associated penalties and interest may become recoverable. Taxpayers are therefore encouraged to act promptly to secure the available relief.
 Our CDH’s Tax & Exchange Control team is available to assist taxpayers in assessing their eligibility for the tax amnesty programme, regularising outstanding tax obligations and engaging KRA to access the relief available under the programme.
